To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the catalytic activity of Fe(III)(TPFPP)Cl for the aerobic oxidation of cyclo hexane to cyclohexanol/cyclohexanone is enhanced by the presence of acetaldehyde and that the reaction is enhanced in pressurised CO2, and that the reaction rate takes a maxima at the vicinity of the critical pressure.
the reaction rate of cyclohexan oxidation is enhanced by pressurizing CO2, and that the maximum value of reaction rate is observed in the neighborhood of the critical point of CO2.

the reaction rates of the aerobic oxidation of cyclo- hexane to cyclohexanol in the presence of the Fe(III) complex of 5,10, 15,20-tetra(pentafluoropheyl)porphynrin (TPFPP) and acetaldehyde in sub- and super-critical CO2 were significantly enhanced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel catalytic system that is capable of performing aerobic oxidation of hydrocarbons in sub- and super-critical CO2.
the development of a new method for aerobic oxidation of cycloaliphatic hydrocarbons in sub- and super-critical CO2.
the development of a novel catalyst system that is active and selective in the aerobic oxidation of alkanes in pressurized carbon dioxide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reaction rate of the aerobic oxidation of cyclo hexane catalyzed by Fe-porphyrins in sub- and supercritical CO2 is enhanced by the presence of acetaldehyde and is maximized near the critical pressure.
the catalytic activity in supercritical CO2 is higher than that in the subcritical state, and the catalytic activity is further improved with the increasing of the pressure.
the reaction rate is enhanced by the increase of the density of supercritical CO2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reaction rate is enhanced in supercritical CO2, while the selectivity for ketone is improved in sub-critical CO2.
the Fe(III) catalyst is more effective for the oxidation in the sub-critical region than the super-critical region.
the catalytic oxidation of hydrocarbons in pressurized gases, such as CO2, is a promising reaction for the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction rate of cyclohexan oxidation in pressurized carbon dioxide is significantly enhanced in the neighborhood of the critical point of carbon dioxide.
the use of CO2 as a solvent and/or reaction medium is a promising way to develop a green oxidation system.
a reaction in pressurized supercritical CO2 can be accelerated to a level comparable to or even higher than that in the presence of organic solvent.
